item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Conceptually, this feels pretty fun but too … perfunctory? Like, there's a lot of interesting concepts touched on here: e.g, the idea of a 'thing in itself', the idea that maybe Nobody is one (or at least, is like one), and the idea of the thing disappearing, possibly after being stolen or because it changed form.

But…none of these are explored in any real depth? There's no philosophical debate or real narrative here so it just feels extremely cursory. I'm left wanting more, rather than feeling satisfied.

item.title: Re: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Whoa this is weird. I like it, but most of it went over my head. I think I have to read it a few more times, but good characterization. It shows how increasingly paranoid this guy is/becomes. Also the concept of thing-in-itself is so strange, it doesn't really have a basis in reality. How can an apple not be an apple if it isn't what we see as an apple? Then it would be something else entirely. :/ ugh confuzzled
+1

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for Calibri Bold and TheBlueHour for looking over the original draft.

This is based on Kant's philosophy of the thing in itself. How much this actually is Kant's thing-in-itself is up for you to decide.
